title: Agent Development Kit (ADK) — official site
quote: The open-source agent development framework that lets you build, debug, and deploy reliable AI agents at enterprise scale. Languages: Python (pip install google-adk), TypeScript/JavaScript (npm install @google/adk), Go (go get google.golang.org/adk), Java (com.google.adk:google-adk), Kotlin (com.google.adk:google-adk-kotlin-core). ADK Go 2.0 GA is live, featuring graph workflows and collaborative agents.

title: Technical Overview — ADK docs
quote: Agent: the foundational execution unit; LlmAgent for reasoning-heavy work, workflow agents (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent) as deterministic controllers. Runner: manages the execution flow, orchestrates agent interactions based on Events, and coordinates with backend services. Event: the basic unit of communication representing things that happen during a session.

title: Agents — ADK docs
quote: An agent is a self-contained execution unit designed to act autonomously to achieve specific goals, combining an AI model, task instructions, and optionally, a set of tools. Any agent application that has more than one agent or executable Node is considered a workflow.

title: Conversational Context: Session, State, and Memory — ADK docs
quote: Session represents a single, ongoing interaction between a user and your agent system. Memory represents a store of information that might span multiple past sessions or include external data sources. SessionService handles the lifecycle of conversation threads; MemoryService manages the long-term knowledge store. In-memory options are designed specifically for local testing and fast development — all data is lost when your application restarts.

title: Graph-based agent workflows — ADK docs
quote: Graph-based workflows allow you to define your agent logic as a graph of execution nodes and edges, combining AI-powered agent reasoning with deterministic tools and code. Conditional routing uses workflow.StringRoute, workflow.IntRoute, or workflow.BoolRoute matched against event.Routes. Supported in ADK Python v2.0.0, Go v2.0.0.

title: Template agent workflows — ADK docs
quote: SequentialAgent executes sub-agents one after another, in sequence. ParallelAgent executes multiple sub-agents in parallel. LoopAgent repeatedly executes its sub-agents until a specific termination condition is met. They determine the execution sequence according to their type without consulting an AI model — this approach results in deterministic and predictable execution patterns.

title: AI Models for ADK agents — ADK docs
quote: ADK is designed for flexibility, allowing you to integrate various Large Language Models into your agents. Native (direct string/registry): Gemini, Claude, Agent Platform endpoints — ADK's internal registry resolves this string. Wrapper-based connectors: Apigee (ApigeeLlm), LiteLLM (LiteLlm), Ollama, vLLM, LiteRT-LM — for broader compatibility, especially models outside the Google ecosystem.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) — ADK docs
quote: An ADK agent can act as an MCP client and use tools provided by external MCP servers. Docs also cover how to build an MCP server that wraps ADK tools, making them accessible to any MCP client. Python-side implementation leverages FastMCP: in most cases, decorating a function is all you need.

title: ADK with Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol — ADK docs
quote: Guides cover how to expose your agent so that other agents can use it via the A2A protocol, and how to allow your agent to use another, remote agent using A2A protocol. Intro demonstrates a multi-agent system with a root agent, a local sub-agent, and a remote A2A agent. Supported in ADK Python, Go, Java. Protocol docs at a2a-protocol.org.

title: Python quickstart — ADK docs
quote: pip install google-adk. adk create my_agent generates my_agent/ with agent.py, .env, __init__.py. root_agent = Agent(model='gemini-flash-latest', name='root_agent', ..., tools=[get_current_time]). adk run my_agent launches an interactive CLI; adk web --port 8000 starts a development server — not meant for use in production deployments.

title: Deploy agents — ADK docs
quote: Agent Runtime on Agent Platform: a fully managed auto-scaling service on Google Cloud specifically designed for deploying, managing, and scaling AI agents. Cloud Run: managed auto-scaling compute platform to run your agent as a container-based application. GKE: more control over the deployment as well as for running Open Models. Also: any container-friendly infrastructure.

title: Why evaluate agents — ADK docs
quote: Due to the probabilistic nature of models, deterministic 'pass/fail' assertions are often unsuitable for evaluating agent performance. Evaluate Trajectory and Tool Use; Evaluate the Final Response. adk eval <AGENT_MODULE> <EVAL_SET_FILE>. Defaults: tool_trajectory_avg_score: 1.0, response_match_score: 0.8. Criteria include ROUGE similarity, LLM-judged equivalence, rubrics, hallucination detection, safety checks.

title: Welcome to ADK 2.0 — ADK docs
quote: ADK 2.0 introduces graph-based workflows, dynamic workflows, and collaborative workflows. Python v2.0.0 GA since May 19, 2026; Go v2.0.0 GA since June 30, 2026. The framework transitioned from a hierarchical agent executor to a graph-based execution engine — agents, tools, and functions now function as individual nodes within a workflow graph.

title: google/adk-python
quote: An open-source, code-first Python toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying sophisticated AI agents with flexibility and control. License: Apache-2.0. Stars: 20,400 (2026-07-02). Latest release v2.3.0 (2026-06-18).

title: google/adk-go
quote: An open-source, code-first Go toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying sophisticated AI agents. Apache-2.0. Stars: 8,325. Latest release v2.0.0 (2026-06-30).

title: google/adk-samples (+ sibling SDK repos)
quote: A collection of sample agents built with Agent Development Kit (ADK). Apache-2.0, 9,807 stars. Sibling SDKs (GitHub API, 2026-07-02): adk-java 1,628 stars; adk-js 1,259 stars (npm @google/adk v1.3.0); adk-kotlin 119 stars — all Apache-2.0.

title: Agent Development Kit: Making it easy to build multi-agent applications
quote: (2025-04-09) An open-source framework from Google designed to simplify the full stack end-to-end development of agents and multi-agent systems. ADK is the same framework powering agents within Google products like Agentspace and the Google Customer Engagement Suite (CES). Deploy to any container runtime or using its integration with Vertex AI Agent Engine — fully managed, scalable, and enterprise-grade runtime. Built-in streaming with bidirectional audio and video streaming capabilities.

title: Google Releases Open-Source Agent Development Kit for Multi-Agent AI Applications
quote: (2025-04-14, announced at Google Cloud Next 2025) The framework is already powering internal systems like Agentspace and the Customer Engagement Suite. Local testing via CLI and web-based UI with execution tracing. AI researcher Cherokee Schill raised governance concerns: 'What happens when systems begin to act with autonomy... Who defines the orchestration logic?'

title: Google Launches Agent Development Kit for Go
quote: (2025-11-25) Google added Go language support to ADK; language lineup at that time: Java, Python, and Go. Built-in development UI (ADK web). With A2A, a primary agent can seamlessly orchestrate and delegate tasks to specialized sub-agents... ensuring secure and opaque interactions.

title: Safety and Security for AI Agents — ADK docs
quote: Sources of risk include vague instructions, model hallucination, jailbreaks and prompt injections from adversarial users, and indirect prompt injections via tool use. Before Tool Callback can be used to add pre-validation of calls. Sandboxing must be used to prevent model-generated code to compromise the local environment. VPC-SC perimeters guarantee that all API calls will only be manipulating resources within the perimeter.

title: Agent Development Kit — Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform docs
quote: An open-source agent development framework that lets you build, debug, and deploy reliable AI agents at enterprise scale. Available in Python, TypeScript, Go, and Java. Run agents locally or scale them globally using Runtime, Cloud Run, or Google Kubernetes Engine. Quickstarts: manage sessions with ADK; ADK quickstart under Memory Bank.

title: Google ADK vs LangGraph vs CrewAI: Agent Frameworks Compared (2026)
quote: ADK: hierarchical tree structure with parent-child agent delegation; best enterprise option, especially for teams that need multi-language SDKs. MCP: all three support it. A2A: only ADK has native support. Weaknesses: steeper learning curve than CrewAI; smaller community; lock-in risk with Google Cloud ecosystem.

title: Best Multi-Agent Frameworks in 2026: LangGraph, CrewAI, ...
quote: An ADK agent can discover and invoke an agent built with LangGraph or CrewAI (via A2A). Natively process images, audio, and video through Gemini's multimodal API. Weaknesses: fewer third-party tutorials, integrations, and production case studies compared to LangGraph or CrewAI; optimized for Gemini models and Vertex AI, limiting flexibility for multi-cloud strategies. Production readiness: early.

title: Upgrading Google ADK to 2.0 on a Cloud SQL Postgres Backend: The Three Things That Bit Us
quote: ADK 2.0 added two required JSONB columns (input_transcription, output_transcription) to the events table. The symptom is not a clear startup crash — the container boots fine, /health returns 200 — but every chat turn 500s. The v0-to-v1 migration cannot be performed in-place; event data storage is restructured from pickled bytea columns to a unified JSONB field.

title: google/adk-python · Issue #3343: Update database schema automatically
quote: ADK 1.14.0 and 1.17.0 introduced breaking database schema changes requiring manual intervention. 'We as the users are obliged to manually update the schema'; 'required changes were not even mentioned and I had to manually find out'. Issue open, no automatic migration mechanism.
